name: What Happens in the First Week of a Kitchen Remodel?

mainEntity.name: What should I expect during the first week of a kitchen remodel with a contractor?
mainEntity.text: What should I expect during the first week of a kitchen remodel with a contractor?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first week is often the most disruptive part of a kitchen remodel. It usually starts with protecting nearby rooms, setting up dust barriers, disconnecting utilities as needed, and removing existing cabinets, countertops, and finishes. If the project involves layout changes, rough framing, plumbing, or electrical work may begin soon after demolition. You should expect noise, debris, and limited access to the kitchen. A good contractor will tell you when water, power, or gas may be shut off and whether any inspections are expected early in the job. This is also when hidden conditions sometimes appear, so the pace can change quickly if repairs are needed. Ask the contractor for a day-by-day outline of the first week so you know what will happen and when. That helps you prepare meals, move belongings, and reduce stress during the most active phase of the project. Clear expectations at the start often set the tone for the rest of the remodel.
acceptedAnswer.description: The first week usually includes site protection, demolition, debris removal, and the start of rough framing or utility work if the design requires it. You may also lose access to the kitchen quickly. A good contractor explains shutdowns, daily cleanup, and inspection timing up front.
